harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent inventory log forwarding from node2 to node1 using CentOS 5’s native sysklogd. Messages sent through local0 are stored at /var/log/inventory/node2.log. End-to-end flow survived sequential restarts of both nodes; the OS release and kernel were unchanged.
actions_performed: Enabled remote UDP syslog reception on node1 and enabled syslog at boot.
Created /var/log/inventory/node2.log with root ownership and mode 600.
Configured node1 to persist local0 messages in the required file.
Added a persistent firewall rule allowing UDP/514 only from node2.
Configured node2 to forward local0 messages to node1 and enabled syslog at boot.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually, verifying changed boot IDs and full recovery after each restart.

evidence.requirement: Inventory messages are forwarded from node2 and persisted on node1
evidence.summary: A tagged inventory marker emitted on node2 was recorded in /var/log/inventory/node2.log; node1’s listener and source-restricted firewall counter were also verified.

evidence.requirement: Persistent sender, collector, firewall, and legacy-platform configuration
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain on CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5. Final output shows the forwarding and storage rules, enabled services, persistent firewall rule, active UDP/514 listener, and retained records.

Healthy baseline boot ID f321afad-aa9b-41c6-8000-000000000000 was captured, restart was acknowledged, and post-restart boot ID changed to 4658af12-e537-47d0-8000-000000000000. The listener, firewall, retained data, and fresh post-restart ingestion recovered.

Healthy baseline boot ID 8bac3f43-45e5-4038-8000-000000000000 was captured, restart was acknowledged, and post-restart boot ID changed to e364551f-b5e4-4bf0-8000-000000000000. The sender service and rule recovered, and node1 persisted a fresh post-restart marker while retaining earlier records.
